authors: Jaeuk Moon, Jonghwa Shim, Eunbeen Kim and Eenjun Hwang
title: MIFlu: Large Language Model-Based Multimodal Influenza Forecasting Scheme
finding: Two LLMs combine text and time series; the institutional record does not substantiate the draft’s claim of only two baselines.

authors: Sarah C. Kramer and Jeffrey Shaman
title: Development and validation of influenza forecasting for 64 temperate and tropical countries
read_level: Full text, Forecast accuracy and Forecast calibration sections
finding: One-week timing and 25% intensity tolerances are verified. Their separate forecast-accuracy assessments do not establish this project’s joint mean-error screen as deployment certification.

authors: Yuqi Nie, Nam H. Nguyen, Phanwadee Sinthong and Jayant Kalagnanam
title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers
finding: Fixed-seed main results, five-seed supervised robustness; ILI sensitive to layer/width settings.

authors: Ailing Zeng, Muxi Chen, Lei Zhang and Qiang Xu
title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?
finding: Simple linear baselines already challenge complex forecasting models; that broad observation is not new to this project.

title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
read_level: Full paper Appendix A.1–A.2, C and D
finding: Chronological separation, five-run robustness in Table 5, separately measured speed/memory.

title: Time-LLM: Time Series Forecasting by Reprogramming Large Language Models
finding: Reprogramming and prompt prefixes differ from frozen numerical features with a linear readout.

title: CALF: Aligning LLMs for Time Series Forecasting via Cross-modal Fine-Tuning
finding: Cross-modal alignment losses are part of CALF; a project adaptation should not be equated with the original method without fidelity checks.

title: TimeCMA: Towards LLM-Empowered Multivariate Time Series Forecasting via Cross-Modality Alignment
read_level: HTML methods outline and abstract; AAAI paper record
finding: Dual branches align time-series and prompt embeddings. This is a distinct design from the frozen-encoder axis.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
read_level: HTML methods and evaluation outline plus abstract
finding: Quantised numerical pretraining yields probabilistic forecasts. Chronos was not run in this benchmark.

authors: Abhimanyu Das, Weihao Kong, Rajat Sen and Yichen Zhou
title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
finding: TimesFM learns from time-series corpora. It cannot be assessed from failures of frozen language encoders.

title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers
finding: Moirai supports heterogeneous series. Its numerical pretraining is outside the tested encoder configuration.

title: Lag-Llama: Towards Foundation Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
finding: Lag-based probabilistic forecasting motivates explicit uncertainty evaluation. No influenza-specific conclusion was verified at abstract level.

authors: Mingtian Tan, Mike A. Merrill, Vinayak Gupta, Tim Althoff and Thomas Hartvigsen
title: Are Language Models Actually Useful for Time Series Forecasting?
finding: Illness 70/10/20; original data-loaders retained; controlled LLM removal/replacement.

title: Rethinking the Role of LLMs in Time Series Forecasting
read_level: Full HTML outline, abstract and routing discussion
finding: The preprint reports conditional benefits under cross-dataset learning and shift. It argues against universal claims of LLM failure.

title: Conformal prediction interval for dynamic time-series
finding: EnbPI offers approximate coverage under stated dependence conditions. A plug-in interval is not automatically valid for detected peak times.

title: Sequential Predictive Conformal Inference for Time Series
finding: Sequential residual quantile prediction addresses dependence; validation data and assumptions are needed.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
finding: Long-run coverage adaptation differs from per-season conditional coverage or low point error.

authors: Johannes Bracher, Evan L. Ray, Tilmann Gneiting and Nicholas G. Reich
title: Evaluating epidemic forecasts in an interval format
read_level: Full text on interval scoring; linked 2022 correction noted
finding: WIS evaluates predictive intervals. Low PIE alone does not establish probabilistic calibration.

venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems 3
title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
read_level: Full PDF §§2–3 and Appendix C: variation, pairing and sample size
finding: Repeated-run precision does not address all pipeline variation.

title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets
read_level: Full PDF §3.2.2 Holm step-down and sampling definition
finding: Familywise correction; multiple-dataset assumptions do not validate dependent horizon cells.

authors: Rob J. Hyndman and Anne B. Koehler
title: Another look at measures of forecast accuracy
finding: MSE/MAE and large-error sensitivity; scale-dependent measures.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
read_level: Full article https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10499856/, L1/L1.2 and model info sheets
finding: Clean separation throughout preprocessing, modelling and evaluation.

title: Out-of-sample tests of forecasting accuracy: an analysis and review
read_level: Publisher-indexed abstract only. Direct publisher page returned 403; no full-text claim.
finding: Abstract motivates rolling-origin evaluation and multiple test periods.

venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30
title: Attention Is All You Need
finding: Causal masking blocks later positions; local bitwise invariance still needs runtime tests.

title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
read_level: Full article https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5502906/, Introduction and Testing for Equivalence
